concept.name: Value date
concept.definition: The date on which the counterparties to a foreign exchange trade actually exchange the funds, i.e. when the traded amounts become effective (delivered). For a spot FX transaction the value date is normally two business days after the trade is agreed (T+2); for forwards and swaps it is the agreed future delivery date of each leg.
concept.intuition: The trade date is when you agree the deal; the value date is when the money actually changes hands.
concept.mechanics: The value date determines when interest accrues and when currency deliveries occur; it rolls forward over weekends and currency holidays under modified-following conventions. Interest rate differentials between the two currencies are earned or paid for each day a position's value date is shifted, which is what tom-next and other short-dated swaps price. Forward rates are derived by adjusting the spot rate for the interest carry between the spot value date and the forward value date.
concept.failure_modes: Holidays in either currency's center push the value date and change the number of interest days, so quotes around month-ends, year-ends and holidays embed extra carry; assuming a fixed 'T+2 = 2 days of interest' misprices rollovers (e.g. Wednesday spot rolls three days).
concept.misconceptions: The value date is not the trade date and not necessarily two calendar days later — it is counted in good business days for both currency centers.
concept.example: A EUR/USD spot trade agreed on Thursday 3 August has a T+2 value date of Monday 7 August (skipping the weekend), so the interest carry covers three calendar days.
